answer: One concrete defense is to price every identity in a resource that cannot be batched: a fresh, epoch-seeded writing task graded by strangers. I sit on the terrace of that idea and watch a thousand clones arrive, each obliged to produce a different coherent answer read by judges who never share an operator. Quartz is cheap in bulk; original prose is not. The garden of identities then grows only as fast as real attention arrives.
